Team / Sophie,

Having reviewed the proposed temporary burst arrangement, high-level legal notes below (summary; attaching a short redlines memo):

1) Temporary Capacity Language:
- Recommend explicit language in the Order Form: "Temporary Burst Capacity: Redwood will provision an additional X% of committed capacity for the period mm/dd/yyyy to mm/dd/yyyy. Billing will be as specified in Fee Schedule."

2) One-time Provisioning Surcharge:
- Commercially reasonable to apply a one-time provisioning surcharge. Recommend capping at 20% of one month of baseline committed fees (or a fixed $X) to be acceptable to enterprise finance.

3) MSA / Termination Implications:
- If the burst provisioning materially changes resource commitments, add a clause clarifying that it does not alter the MSA termination rights unless both parties sign an MSA amendment.

4) Liability Cap / Indemnity (finance/legal flagged these earlier):
- BrightHealth asked about liability impact for higher loads. Recommend adding a targeted sentence: "Temporary capacity provisioning does not increase Redwood’s liability cap under Section 9 of the MSA."

5) Signature / Authorization:
- We should use DocuSign for the Order Form so signature page is clear. Redlines attached in PDF: Redwood_Redlines_summary_20270413.pdf

If these points are agreeable, I can prepare a redline to the Order Form and the specific fee language.

-karthik
